comparison: Perfect agreement on kinetic measurements (C18-C30). Both evaluations find the DNA length-dependent binding data and quantitative measurements fully supported. OpenEval notes comprehensive kinetic measurements with error estimates; peer reviewers explicitly praise findings as 'exciting and timely' without requesting additional validation.

Perfect agreement on Brownian diffusion on naked DNA (C31-C37). Both evaluations fully support the optical tweezers data and linear MSD analysis. OpenEval highlights appropriate controls (dCas9); peer reviewers call this 'the first conclusive demonstration' of 1D diffusion without requesting additional experiments.

Partial disagreement on ATP-enhanced diffusion mechanism (C38-C46). OpenEval finds the evidence strong and supports conclusions based on ATP/ATPγS/ADP comparisons with statistical testing. Peer reviewers find it 'intriguing' but uncertain, requesting additional experiments to distinguish whether ATP affects the motor subunit directly or acts allosterically on Swc2.

Partial disagreement on Swc2 role and hopping mechanism (C47-C54). OpenEval supports the data but notes C5 is somewhat inferential. Peer reviewers rate as uncertain and request additional experiments with competitor DNA to validate the 'monkey bar' mechanism and distinguish hopping from alternative multi-site binding.

OpenEval R5 addresses mechanistic model integrating theoretical limits (C55-C58), which overlaps with peer R4's concerns about hopping mechanism. OpenEval finds the mixed mechanism model reasonable; peer reviewers want additional validation of the hopping interpretation through competitor DNA experiments.

Perfect agreement on dCas9 blocking experiments (C59-C62). Both evaluations support the conclusion that 97% blocking demonstrates predominantly sliding diffusion. OpenEval praises the programmable barrier design; peer reviewers accept findings without critique or requests for additional validation.

Disagreement on nucleosome interaction characterization (C63-C75). OpenEval supports the confinement analysis but notes C75 is somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers rate as uncertain and request more detailed description, labeled nucleosomes, and quantification of immobile molecules to enable 'more confident conclusions' about SWR1-nucleosome interactions.

Disagreement on functional significance and scanning time calculations (C7-C8, C77, C99). OpenEval supports the calculation methodology despite noting a discrepancy (46 ms vs 93 ms). Peer reviewers rate as uncertain, requesting more quantitative discussion of the 1D search effect magnitude and noting the model 'does not explain' differential +1/-1 nucleosome targeting.

Agreement on speculative nature of in vivo model (C96-C100). OpenEval rates as uncertain, noting the 'antenna' model is plausible but lacks direct in vivo evidence. Peer reviewers similarly note it 'does not establish whether these properties are required' in vivo and request acknowledgment that further work is needed.

Perfect agreement on methodological validation (C83-C87). Both evaluations fully support the labeling strategy and activity controls. OpenEval emphasizes this as critical validation; peer reviewers accept without critique or requests for additional validation.

Perfect agreement on background literature claims (C1, C9-C17 in OpenEval; broader set in peer R12 including C88-C98). Both evaluations support these as appropriately cited established knowledge providing necessary context. No validation concerns raised by either evaluation.

Perfect agreement on prior in vivo literature (C76-C82). Both evaluations support these as appropriately cited established findings. OpenEval notes they contextualize current findings; peer reviewers accept as framework without requesting validation.

Perfect agreement on SWR1 structural/mechanistic background (C88-C91). Both evaluations support these literature-based claims. OpenEval notes they provide context for ATP effects; peer reviewers accept as established framework.
Perfect agreement on biophysical principles (C92-C95). Both evaluations support these as appropriately cited theoretical framework from literature. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Perfect agreement on in vivo complexity caveats (C103-C105). Both evaluations support these as established considerations. OpenEval notes they highlight limitations; peer reviewers acknowledge these as accepted features affecting the model.

OpenEval R15 partially overlaps with peer R10 on in vivo targeting complexities (C101-C102). OpenEval supports these as important caveats; peer reviewers emphasize these limitations more strongly in their uncertainty rating for the broader in vivo model.

Perfect agreement on methodological calculations (C106-C109 overlap, C110 in peer R13). Both evaluations support the localization precision and DNA length calculations. OpenEval notes appropriate formulas; peer reviewers praise the 'extremely elegant' optical tweezers approach without questioning technical details.
